source_label: Diablo Weather Labs · Nov 19 morning briefing + NWS Bay Area and Sacramento forecast discussions

Moraga.headline: Another burst of rain and a few rumbles before a sharply colder finish
Moraga.text: A fresh band of rain crosses Moraga this morning, and the unsettled weather is not finished: additional showers may turn briefly heavy today, with an isolated thunderstorm, small hail or a strong gust possible. With the ground already saturated, even a short downpour could renew ponding and drainage problems, so watch for water on roads and in low spots. Showers should gradually become less frequent tonight into Friday, but colder air brings a chilly Friday and Saturday morning. A weaker system may bring another round of showers this weekend, with a more significant, still uncertain storm possible Tuesday into Wednesday.

Lafayette.headline: A wet Thursday gives way to a cold valley morning and another weekend shower chance
Lafayette.text: Reliez Valley is in the path of another round of rain this morning, followed by hit-or-miss showers that could briefly become heavy today. A few thunderstorms, small hail and gusty outflows are possible, while saturated ground means even a localized downpour could cause fresh street or drainage issues. The rain should ease gradually later today and tonight, leaving a much colder start Friday and another chilly morning Saturday. A weaker disturbance could bring additional showers this weekend, then attention turns to a potentially wetter Tuesday–Wednesday system whose track and local rainfall remain uncertain.

Danville.headline: Showers may flare again today, with a colder and unsettled stretch ahead
Danville.text: Another wave of rain is moving through the Danville area this morning, and scattered showers should continue into the afternoon as colder air swings across the Bay Area. Brief downpours, isolated thunder, small hail and locally strong gusts are possible; after Wednesday’s soaking, any heavier burst could quickly create ponding on streets and in poor-drainage spots. Rain should taper tonight, followed by a distinctly colder Friday and Saturday morning. A weaker system may brush the valley with showers this weekend, while a broader storm signal is emerging for Tuesday and Wednesday.

Greenbrook.headline: A final round of downpours could bring thunder before the valley turns colder
Greenbrook.text: Greenbrook faces another unsettled day as a fresh rain band moves through this morning and scattered showers linger into the afternoon. A few stronger cells could produce a brief downpour, small hail, lightning or a sharp wind gust, so saturated streets and drainage areas deserve extra attention. Conditions should gradually improve tonight and Friday, but the colder air behind the system will make Friday and Saturday mornings feel markedly colder. A weaker disturbance could bring a few showers back this weekend, with another potentially wetter system taking shape for Tuesday into Wednesday.

Marin City.headline: Coastal showers and blustery winds linger as colder air moves in
Marin City.text: Marin City is seeing another push of rain this morning, with showers and occasional heavier bursts possible through the afternoon as the storm’s colder core moves across the coast. The marine setting keeps the day cool and damp, while exposed areas may feel stronger, shifting winds; an isolated thunderstorm or small hail cannot be ruled out. With soils already saturated, brief heavy rain could aggravate runoff and localized flooding. Showers should ease gradually tonight, but colder mornings follow, and a weaker weekend system may bring more rain before a potentially wetter storm arrives Tuesday or Wednesday.

Sausalito.headline: Wind-driven showers keep the waterfront unsettled before a colder weekend
Sausalito.text: Sausalito remains on the windy, showery side of the storm this morning, with another band of rain crossing the Bay Area and scattered showers likely to continue into the afternoon. The waterfront’s marine exposure will keep conditions cool and breezy, and stronger showers could bring a sudden gust, small hail or an isolated rumble of thunder. Saturated ground raises the risk of renewed ponding, while hazardous surf continues along the open coast through early Friday. Rain should ease later, but colder mornings are ahead, with another weaker shower-maker possible this weekend.

Brentwood.headline: The Delta could see a stormier afternoon as heavy rain shifts east
Brentwood.text: Rain is moving across the Delta this morning, but Brentwood’s weather story may not end when the main band passes: breaks and daytime heating could help isolated afternoon thunderstorms develop. The strongest cells could bring torrential bursts, lightning, small hail and gusty winds, with the Delta more exposed to strong southerly flow than sheltered inland neighborhoods. Saturated ground and strong Delta winds heighten impacts, while low-lying areas remain vulnerable to flooding. Showers should diminish tonight, followed by colder weather; another, weaker system may bring valley rain this weekend before a more uncertain Tuesday–Wednesday storm.

East Sacramento.headline: Morning rain gives way to a break, but isolated Valley storms remain possible
East Sacramento.text: Periods of rain are moving through the Sacramento Valley this morning, with the steadiest precipitation expected to shift east and become more scattered later today. As skies brighten, inland heating may help a few showers grow into thunderstorms, although the strongest storm chances are favored farther south; any cell could still bring lightning, a gusty burst or small hail. Watch for ponding where yesterday’s rain has overwhelmed drainage. Friday trends drier, then colder nights and some morning fog become more likely, with a weaker weekend system and another unsettled period possible Tuesday into Wednesday.
